nodes.content: Develop offline policy improvement certificates that remain valid under bounded hidden confounding without requiring full action coverage.
requirements: Certificates attain at least 95% coverage of true policy gains under the stated confounding bound.
Certify strictly positive gains over the behavior policy in a nontrivial, explicitly characterized regime.

nodes.content: Develop overlap-gated contextual-bandit policies with Γ-constrained propensity-weight gain bounds and 95% holdout intervals; certify only positive lower bounds.
Under Γ=1.5, how large must overlap-region reward margins be for a 95% lower gain bound to exceed zero?
At Γ=1.5, targeted-action propensity ≥0.1 and sensitivity-adjusted margin ≥0.15 yield positive certificates in ≥80% of 5,000-sample trials.
Simulate 1,000 confounded 5,000-sample bandits at Γ=1.5; vary overlap and margins, measuring gain coverage and positive-certificate rates.
Run 1,000 5,000-sample Γ=1.5 bandit replicates with unavailable actions; sweep propensities and margins, measuring gain coverage and certification rates.
In 1,000 Γ=1.5 5,000-sample replicates, true-gain coverage reached 96.2%; propensity ≥0.1 and adjusted margin ≥0.15 yielded 84% positive certificates.
Advance overlap-gated Γ=1.5 certificates to benchmark validation; simulated 96.2% coverage and 84% high-margin certification justify progression.
ConfoundBandit-v1: reproducible 1,000-replicate simulation suite with Γ=1.5 sensitivity settings, coverage tables, and propensity-margin certification curves.
Using ConfoundBandit-v1, simulate 1,000 held-out 5,000-sample Γ=1.5 bandits near propensity 0.1/margin 0.15; test ≥95% coverage and ≥80% certification.
Across 1,000 held-out replicates, coverage was 95.8%, but propensity ≥0.1 and adjusted margin ≥0.15 yielded only 63% positive certificates.
At Γ=1.5, propensity ≥0.2 and adjusted margin ≥0.20 yield ≥80% positive certificates at 5,000 samples, retaining ≥95% coverage.
Run 1,000 independent ConfoundBandit-v1 trials (n=5,000; Γ=1.5) with unavailable actions; test ≥95% coverage and ≥80% certification at revised thresholds.
Independent Γ=1.5 trials achieved 95.6% true-gain coverage and 87% positive certificates at propensity ≥0.2, adjusted margin ≥0.20.
Develop Γ-robust Bellman advantage certificates with simultaneous 95% intervals; switch only at supported state–action pairs, otherwise retain behavior.
What occupancy-shift bound lets locally positive Γ-robust Bellman advantages certify global improvement despite unsupported state–action pairs?
Derive Γ-robust performance-difference bounds under state-occupancy ratio caps; test 95% coverage and positive certification on sparse-action MDPs.
Extend ConfoundBandit-v1 to sparse-action MDPs; compare overlap-gated and occupancy-capped Bellman certificates at Γ=1.5 for coverage and positive-certification rates.
At Γ=1.5, overlap-gated coverage was 91% on sparse-action bandits; occupancy-capped Bellman coverage was 96% on sparse-action MDPs, certifying 73%.
Reanalyze n16's sparse-action MDP trials; sweep occupancy-ratio caps 1.2–3.0 and measure Bellman-certificate coverage and positive-certification rates.
OccupancyCap-v1: reproducible cap 1.2–3.0 sweep tables and Γ=1.5 Bellman-certificate coverage and positive-certification curves.
Audit OccupancyCap-v1 on 1,000 held-out Γ=1.5 sparse-action MDPs, checking occupancy-cap validity, gain coverage, and positive-certification rates.
At Γ=1.5 and occupancy cap 2.0, 1,000 held-out MDPs showed 95.8% gain coverage, 71% positive certification, and 99% cap validity.
Retain overlap-gated certificates for high-margin bandits; prioritize occupancy-capped Bellman certificates for sparse MDPs, conditional on verified caps.
Use randomized encouragement to certify Γ-robust policy gains in supported strata, retaining behavior elsewhere and requiring no action coverage.
At n=5,000, valid encouragement with ≥20% compliance yields ≥95% gain coverage and certifies positive gains for Γ=1.5-adjusted margins ≥0.2.
When does an encouragement-based complier effect lower-bound policy gain across all patients in supported strata?
Extend ConfoundBandit-v1 with randomized encouragement; vary compliance and noncomplier effects, testing Γ=1.5 complier-based gain coverage and positive certification.
At Γ=1.5, 20% compliance and adjusted complier margins of 0.2 yielded only 82% policy-gain coverage with adverse noncomplier effects.
Derive Γ=1.5 complier-weighted bounds with explicit noncomplier-harm limits; simulate compliance and harm sweeps to test 95% policy-gain coverage.
Simulate 1,000 ConfoundBandit-v1 trials (n=5,000; Γ=1.5; margin ≥0.2), sweeping compliance and noncomplier-harm caps; measure gain coverage and certification.
With compliance ≥20%, noncomplier harm ≤0.02, and adjusted margins ≥0.2, harm-capped bounds achieved 96.1% coverage and 76% positive certification.
How can the noncomplier-harm cap of 0.02 be justified when encouragement data do not identify noncomplier treatment effects?
A randomized audit of 6,000 identified noncompliers yields 95% harm bounds ≤0.02 in ≥85% of trials when true harm ≤0.005.
Extend n25 adverse-effect and n28 harm-capped simulations with 1,000 randomized audits of 6,000 preidentified noncompliers; test 95%-coverage and ≤0.02-attainment.
Across 1,000 randomized audits of 6,000 preidentified noncompliers, harm-bound coverage was 96%; 88% attained ≤0.02 when true harm ≤0.005.
Integrate adverse-effect scenarios, harm-capped bounds, and randomized-audit limits; test jointly calibrated 95% policy-gain coverage across 1,000 trials.
EncouragementAudit-v1: jointly calibrated 95% Γ=1.5 gain-bound code integrating noncomplier-harm audits, adverse-effect scenarios, and 1,000-trial validation tables.
Develop Γ-sensitive matched-set linear programs for 95% lower gain bounds; retain behavior outside matched, action-supported strata.
How can Γ-sensitive matched-set bounds cover whole-population policy gains when unmatched strata retain behavior but matching distorts stratum weights?
Estimate population stratum weights independently; aggregate Γ-sensitive matched-set bounds, assign zero gains to unmatched strata, and calibrate 95% intervals.
Adapt EncouragementAudit-v1’s joint calibration to matched-set LPs with independent population weights; test Γ=1.5 sparse-action gain coverage and certification.
Across 1,000 Γ=1.5 sparse-action trials, matched-set LPs covered 91% of true gains; matching-induced dependence invalidated interval calibration.
Can sample-split matching and weight estimation restore 95% gain coverage without eliminating positive certificates in supported strata?
Three-way splitting of matching, LP evaluation, and population-weight estimation restores ≥95% gain coverage and ≥60% positive certification at Γ=1.5.
Using EncouragementAudit-v1 calibration, run 1,000 Γ=1.5 sparse-action trials with disjoint matching, LP, and weight folds; assess coverage and certification.
Three-way-split matched-set LPs achieved 95.7% gain coverage and 64% positive certificates across 1,000 Γ=1.5 sparse-action trials.
Using EncouragementAudit-v1 calibration, compare dependent versus three-way-split matched LPs; test population-weighted coverage and positive certification with unmatched gains zero.
Population-weighted split LPs covered 95.5% of whole-population gains and certified 62% positive; dependent matching covered 90.8%.
MatchedGain-v1: three-way-split Γ=1.5 LP implementation, independent population-weight estimator, and zero-gain handling for unmatched strata.
Develop negative-control proxy-assisted Γ-robust gain bounds with split-calibrated 95% intervals; change actions only in supported strata.
What proxy-strength and negative-control validity conditions permit narrower Γ=1.5 gain bounds without sacrificing 95% coverage?
Bound negative-control violations and proxy bridge error, then jointly calibrate Γ=1.5 gain intervals across proxy-strength sweeps and sparse-action strata.
Use OccupancyCap-v1 and MatchedGain-v1 to benchmark Γ=1.5 negative-control bounds; sweep proxy strength and violations, measuring coverage, width, certification.
With proxy correlation ≥0.7 and negative-control bias ≤0.01, Γ=1.5 intervals covered 95.8% of gains and narrowed 22% versus MatchedGain-v1.
Adapt EncouragementAudit-v1’s calibration to n49’s strong-proxy regime; sweep control violations 0–0.03, checking ≥95% gain coverage and positive-certification rates.
ProxyGain-v1: jointly calibrated Γ=1.5 gain intervals, proxy-strength and negative-control-bias sweeps, and sparse-action certification tables.
Audit ProxyGain-v1 against occupancy-capped, dependent-match, and split-match baselines on 1,000 Γ=1.5 strong-proxy sparse-action trials; test ≥95% coverage and positive certification.
Across 1,000 strong-proxy Γ=1.5 trials, ProxyGain-v1 covered 95.9% of true gains and certified 78% positive, versus split-match 62%.
Prioritize ProxyGain-v1 with proxy correlation ≥0.7 and control bias ≤0.01; otherwise use split-match, rejecting under-covering dependent matching.
ProxyGain-Audit-v1: reproducible 1,000-trial Γ=1.5 benchmark report documenting 95.9% gain coverage, 78% positive certification, and split-match comparisons.
